svg.text: Figure 1. Spatial Architecture of Macro-Region I (Ob-Irtysh Basin), Archaeological Complexes & Yugra Principalities
Sub-Regions I-1 (Altai), I-2 (Southern Steppe & Forest-Steppe) and I-3 (NW Siberian Taiga-Tundra & Ten Ob-Ugrian Principalities, 10000 BC – 1700 AD)
Palaeolithic / Neolithic Complexes (10000–4000 BC: Amnya I, Kayukovo 2)
Eneolithic & Bronze Age Megasites (3700–800 BC: Botai, Arkaim, Chicha-1)
Early Iron Age & Scythian-Sargat Centres (800 BC–500 AD: Pazyryk, Ust-Polui)
Medieval Khanate & Arctic Fortresses (800–1600 AD: Isker, Sherkaly-1, Nadym)
Ten Ob-Ugrian (Yugra) Principalities (12th–17th c. AD; Dolgikh 1960):
1 Pelym • 2 Tabary • 3 Kondia • 4 Kod (Koda) • 5 Belogorye • 6 Kazym
7 Sosva • 8 Lyapin & Kunovat • 9 Obdorsk • 10 Bardakovo & Surgut Ob
Sources: Bakhrushin (1935); Dolgikh (1960); Matveeva (2000); Piezonka et al. (2023).
Total Area: ~2 395 000 km² | Pre-Russian Peak (1000 AD): ~241 000 inhabitants | 1580 AD Indigenous Total: ~163 500 | 1700 AD Total: ~269 000
